question: Which of the following is NOT an output device for a computer?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Scanner**__**.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A scanner converts physical documents or images into digital format for **electronic storage or manipulation.**
 
• Common types of scanners include flatbed, sheet-fed, handheld, and drum scanners, each serving different purposes.
 
• Measured in DPI (dots per inch), a higher DPI indicates better image clarity and detail in the** scanned output.**
 
• **Optical resolution** is the actual capability of the scanner’s sensor, while software resolution can enhance image quality through interpolation techniques.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Monitor**

 
 
• A monitor is an output device used to **display images, videos, and text generated **by a computer or other electronic devices.
 
• Common types of monitors include **LCD (Liquid Crystal Display)**, **LED (Light Emitting Diode**), and **OLED (Organic LED)**, with varying energy efficiency and display quality.
 
• Monitor resolution is measured in pixels (e.g., 1920x1080), with higher resolutions providing clearer and more detailed images.
 
 
 
• **Printer**
 
 
• Printer is an **output device** that transfers digital text and images onto paper or other physical media.
 
• Common printer types include inkjet (suitable for high-quality color printing), laser (fast and efficient for text-heavy documents), and 3D printers (used for creating three-dimensional objects).
 
• Print quality is measured in **DPI (dots per inch**), with higher DPI providing sharper and more detailed printed output.
 
 
 
• **Projector**
 
 
• A projector is an **output device **that projects images, videos, or presentations onto a larger screen or surface, making it suitable for classrooms, meetings, and home theaters.
 
• Common types of projectors include **LCD (Liquid Crystal Display)**,** DLP (Digital Light Processing**), and **LED projectors**, each with different technologies and use cases.
 
• Projector quality is often measured in terms of resolution (e.g., 1080p) and brightness (measured in lumens), with higher values providing clearer images in various lighting conditions.
